summary: Sketch drags are now answered by the app's own native solver first, so dragging no longer loads PlaneGCS. A drag becomes two temporary value relations on the dragged point, after the sketch's relations. Native answers a drag whose target was reached or projected when the result is converged, fully diagnosed, keeps fixed source geometry and passes the graph checks, as for any other solve. Projected means the native solver's first- and second-order necessary conditions for a local minimum of the distance to the target held up to its documented resolution; it proves neither a local minimum nor the nearest configuration, and higher orders are unchecked. A drag that stalls is not converged, and PlaneGCS is asked instead, the stalled rejection standing when PlaneGCS does no better. A drag diagnosed as conflicting or redundant where it ended, such as a point landed exactly on a tangency, is also tried with PlaneGCS first, since that rank describes the landing and not the sketch. PlaneGCS also still answers drags whose rank native cannot yet diagnose, such as some nearly straight arms stretched beyond their reach. A drag moves its point's groups on purpose, so they are never kept at their start values, and a reached target is kept exactly. For the die, from medians of interleaved Node runs at about 65 to 75 ms of calibration, a drag falls from about 1.73 to 1.53 ms, and the first drag after native solves from about 19 to 6.2 ms because PlaneGCS is no longer loaded for it. PlaneGCS still loads for the solves native cannot answer.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. Dragged geometry can differ from PlaneGCS's, in the last digits or, after a large single jump, by a different constrained configuration: where PlaneGCS reassembles a linkage the other way up and ends closer to the target, native stays on the assembly the drag started from. A projected result passes the native solver's local checks; it does not prove that the target is unreachable or that no closer configuration exists. Editor preview frames still solve from the drag-start document. A drag that neither solver can move is rejected with the message that the point could not be moved toward the target from this start.

checklist.schema: No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, CAD, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol schema change. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation or input-version behavior change. WebMCP tools keep their arguments and result fields.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change and no new application controls.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change.
checklist.verification: Runtime tests cover solves and drags answered natively without loading PlaneGCS, a reached drag target kept exactly however little it moved, a two-link arm dragged out of reach and back, chained and from the start, reached natively within reach and ending as close to its targets as PlaneGCS beyond it, where PlaneGCS answers the stretched frames native cannot diagnose, a stalled drag rejected as not moved unless PlaneGCS solves it, a point dragged onto a tangency that native would call redundant solved by PlaneGCS with native's rejection standing otherwise, and a four-bar dragged out of reach in one jump that native answers on its starting assembly, stretched at c = (-2.8, 9.6), 32.52 mm from the target, deterministically and as when chained over ten frames. Compilation tests cover the two temporary value equations after the relations and reject a missing point, a coordinate beyond 1e9 mm and a non-finite target. The native-differential project now compares drags too: every native drag must end within max(1e-6, 64 epsilon S) mm of PlaneGCS's distance to its target unless it is a reviewed change of assembly, named by test, point and target, whose native position is recorded and which fails when it no longer differs. The one reviewed case is that four-bar, which PlaneGCS reassembles in one jump to 19.14 mm but, dragged in ten steps, ends where native does. Across the suites 38 drags were compared directly and 24 answered by the runtime, none stalled, and none ended further than PlaneGCS beyond that allowance except the reviewed four-bar. Timings are medians of three interleaved sets of 40 runs and seven cold probes in fresh processes.

publicNotes.summary: Drags sketches with the app's own solver.
changes: Answers sketch drags with the app's own solver, so the first drag starts sooner and later drags are slightly faster.
Large drags of linkages keep the assembly they started in, and can settle in a different place from earlier releases.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged.
